rationale: The experience register is a library of small reusable user experiences — component contracts and micro-journeys — held once and forked per site, so that a link has a declared intended destination and an acceptance test can be derived rather than invented. This submission is P2a: the substrate plus the one piece of logic everything else depends on. Two things a reviewer should weigh it against. FIRST, the shape was harvested, not designed: nine entries were taken from live implementations on two sites on 2026-07-26, and every column below the taxonomy axes exists because a working implementation needed it and the 2026-07-24 design could not express it — `states` because the most valuable clause in the harvested code is 'this must NOT be a control'; `degraded_states` because a failure path is where dishonesty enters a page; `automatic_triggers` because four of the nine harvested behaviours are triggered by the viewport or a system preference rather than by a visitor; `requires_invariant` because ONE rule turned up in six independent implementations across two sites and five authors, and copying it into each entry would industrialise the drift instead of ending it. SECOND, the validator answers three failure classes that are live today, not hypothetical: criteria are parsed at read time only, so a template asserting markup the page no longer ships looks green while asserting nothing; a template can name a check the platform cannot execute (the council-APPROVED gauntlet EXPERIENCE_PLAN contains two interaction checks that assert 300ms after a click, while the API they wait on takes 8–23 seconds — they parse perfectly, they would fail a correct page, and the tempting repair of painting placeholder text would make them pass with the engine switched off); and a base entry carrying a concrete URL is the bugs_closed/045 class, a static fallback re-applied on every render that a per-site binding cannot override. STATUS, stated plainly because it changes what is worth objecting to: this change is already committed (2f220f261) and migration 218 was applied by hand on 2026-07-27 after chassis v1.0.1172 shipped the Go half. An earlier submission of this same change-set (corr f4610451-6bff-45d0-8d18-6f25d26640cd) never returned a verdict — it wedged at review_editquality and was killed by the 4-hour stale-step reaper, one of eight runs reaped that day. So objections here become follow-up commits rather than edits before landing, and objections to the SCHEMA are the most valuable ones, because a live table is far more expensive to change than unlanded code. No write path exists yet, so no row has been written through it and the tables are empty by design.

plan.summary: Add the experience register's substrate and its write-time criteria validator. Migration 218 creates experience_patterns (the library), site_experiences (per-site forks binding roles to real pages and selectors) and experience_invariants (clauses that hold across many patterns, held once), and adds 'experience-pattern' to the doc_plans/doc_notes subject_type CHECK so each entry carries a travelling doc exactly as a tool does. The Go vocabulary validDocSubjectTypes gains the same value in the same change, because a value the DB accepts and a Go gate rejects is the split contract of migration 184 (bugs_closed/064). experience_criteria.go validates a criteria template at WRITE time: it must parse; every {{binding.x}} placeholder must close against the entry's binding_schema in both directions; no base entry may carry an absolute URL or an unbound site-specific selector; '-EDIT' placeholder ids are rejected outright; and every check must be either executable by a named tier or explicitly marked deferred with a reason. A check beyond the platform is recorded as DEFERRED, never dropped and never counted as a pass. Two mechanical drift guards hold the hand-maintained tables to their sources: one test parses the newest migration that sets the subject CHECK, the other reads the real switch statements out of both checkers.

edits.rationale: The register needs its own table because doc_plans has no site_id, no metadata column and no structured search — it is queried by exact key only, so it can carry an entry's direction and provenance but cannot be selected FROM. Site-agnostic by construction: no URLs and no site-specific selectors in the base entry, because a concrete value baked into a base row is the bugs_closed/045 class. The invariants table exists because one clause was found in six independent implementations; holding it once and referencing it is the difference between ending the drift and industrialising it. Entries are deliberately NOT seeded by raw INSERT — the first rows in the register should be ones the validator accepted, or the register has no proof its own contract holds.
edits.sketch:
BEGIN;
ALTER TABLE doc_plans DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS doc_plans_subject_type_check;
ALTER TABLE doc_plans ADD CONSTRAINT doc_plans_subject_type_check
  CHECK (subject_type = ANY (ARRAY['tool'::text,'pipeline'::text,'experience'::text,'action'::text,'experience-pattern'::text]));
-- same pair for doc_notes

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS experience_invariants (
    name text PRIMARY KEY, clause text NOT NULL, rationale text NOT NULL,
    sightings jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
    status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft','approved')), ...);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS experience_patterns (
    id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    name text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    kind text NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('component-contract','micro-journey')),
    -- selection axes (the component_selector scoring shape transfers)
    primitives jsonb, section_types jsonb, destination_roles jsonb,
    funnel_stage text CHECK (funnel_stage IN ('awareness','consideration','conversion')),
    suitable_site_types jsonb,
    contract jsonb NOT NULL,          -- every trigger names an OBSERVABLE outcome;
                                      -- navigating triggers name a destination ROLE, never a URL
    states jsonb, automatic_triggers jsonb, data_contract jsonb,
    degraded_states jsonb, entry_points jsonb,
    requires_component_contract jsonb, requires_invariant jsonb,
    binding_schema jsonb, criteria_template jsonb,
    status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft','approved','proven')), ...);
    -- draft = visible, UNSELECTABLE; approved = council pass; proven = first live green run

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS site_experiences (
    site_id uuid NOT NULL, pattern_name text NOT NULL REFERENCES experience_patterns(name),
    instance_key text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default', bindings jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'proposed' CHECK (status IN ('proposed','bound','verified','broken')),
    last_checked_at timestamptz, last_check_result jsonb, built_from_plan_version uuid,
    UNIQUE (site_id, pattern_name, instance_key));

-- GIN indexes on the three array axes; seed the two evidenced invariants ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
-- guard DO block asserts both CHECKs list experience-pattern, all three tables exist,
-- both invariants seeded — inside the transaction, so a partial apply rolls itself back.
COMMIT;

edits.rationale: The Go vocabulary and the DB CHECK are ONE contract. Migration 184 widened the CHECK alone and the resulting rows were unreachable through the doc actions for months (bugs_closed/064). Adding the value in the same change is the whole point; the ORDER is still the operator's to get right, and the comment says so.

The owner ruled on 2026-07-24 that approval is per experience and that the acceptance-test side must be formalised. This is that formalisation, and it is the piece every later part depends on: the write path validates on the way in, the bind path re-runs closure against the real bindings, and the consumer runs what survives. The design choice worth reviewing is the treatment of a check the platform cannot execute. Erroring would block a true clause; dropping it would delete the clause from the record, which is how a pattern comes to look fully checked when its most important rule is not checked at all. So it is DEFERRED: declared, carried, reported, and never counted as a pass.

A capability table maintained by hand drifts from the checker within one change, and a validator that believes a stale table waves through exactly the checks it exists to catch. So the table is not trusted: the test reads the real switch statements out of both checkers' source and fails in BOTH directions. This is the third use of the dedup-index idiom (v1.0.1127, bugs_closed/064). Both guards were proved by induced fault before the commit, not merely observed to pass: removing the Go subject-type entry failed the test naming migration 218; adding a bogus check type failed with 'the table says ... but discovery_checks/check_tool_acceptance.go does not implement it'; removing a real one failed with 'the browser runner implements "no_console_errors" but the validator's table does not know it'.

grounded_in: rejects, or vice versa, is a split contract; move both together.
// Confirm the anchors of everything the interaction touches.
time.Sleep(stepDelay) // let handlers/render settle before the next step or assertion
settleDelay       = 2 * time.Second // let JS-built DOM render before asserting
plan.risks: 1. SCHEMA is the expensive half and it is already applied — objections to column shape, to the status vocabularies (draft/approved/proven; proposed/bound/verified/broken), or to holding invariants in a separate table referenced by name rather than inlined per entry, are the ones worth raising hardest. 2. The widened subject_type CHECK is live and the Go half shipped in v1.0.1172 (verified against the running pod: the string is present, a never-existed control returns zero); a reviewer should check the ORDER argument, not just the pair. 3. ValidateExperienceCriteria has NO caller yet — it is dead code until the write path lands, so it is unexercised in production and its rules have only test evidence. That is deliberate (the validator must exist before anything can be written through it) but it means a rule that is subtly wrong will not surface until the first real entry. 4. The capability tables encode a snapshot of what two checkers do TODAY; the lockstep test catches drift in the check-type vocabulary but NOT in semantics — if the browser runner changes what `interaction` means, the table still matches and the validator still passes. 5. The deferral escape hatch is the soft spot: `_unsupported` with a reason is the honest path, but nothing yet stops an author deferring every difficult check and shipping an entry whose criteria assert nothing of substance. A minimum-executable-checks rule at the APPROVAL step, not at write time, is the intended answer; it is not built. 6. Migration 218 shares its number with 218_evidence_facts_for_043_sites.sql — the shop's numbering has several historical duplicates and files are resolved by full name, but it is worth a reviewer's eye.
